request.prompt: View 2, the same camp seen from straight above, a top-down plan view with north at the top of the frame, in late afternoon. The leafy crowns are cut away, as if lifted off, so the platforms, cabins, bridges and trunks are clearly visible from directly above; only a thin ring of chunky leaves marks the edge of each crown. Four giant trees, each a big round blocky trunk seen from above, each wrapped by a square plank platform. Upper left of centre: the Hearth Tree, the biggest, with the biggest square platform, a long thatched cabin and a stone hearth. Upper right: the Loom Tree, with a smaller square platform, a lean-to and cloth lines. Lower left: the Seed Tree, with a small square platform, baskets and a storehouse cabin. Lower right: the Watch Tree, with a medium square platform and a small sentry cabin, and directly over the middle of it a smaller square ring of planks, the lookout, around the top of the trunk. Three straight narrow rope bridges, each running in a perfectly straight line, either exactly left-right or exactly up-down: one runs straight right from the Hearth platform to the Loom platform; one runs straight down from the Hearth platform to the Seed platform; one runs straight down from the Loom platform to the Watch platform. There is no bridge between the Seed Tree and the Watch Tree. Between the trees, far below, the uneven forest floor of moss, ferns, roots and a few fallen logs, darker in the low dell around the Seed Tree at the lower left and on higher ground at the upper right.
request.style_note: The Treehouse Camp, a forest clan's camp of wooden treehouses built around the trunks of four separate giant trees deep in an old temperate forest, joined by rope bridges and rope ladders, drawn in the same hand throughout: warm painterly fantasy concept painting, late-afternoon sun slanting in low gold shafts through a high green canopy, deep moss and fern greens, warm red-brown bark, honey-coloured planks and pale thatch, small warm accents of lantern and fire light, soft forest haze, confident brushwork with crisp readable silhouettes. Everything is massed from large squared blocks with flat faces and clean right angles so every form could be built block by block in Minecraft: the giant trunks are stepped, blocky round columns of bark flaring into blocky buttress roots, the crowns are chunky cubic masses of leaves on thick square branches, the platforms are square plank decks with post-and-rope rails, the huts are small timber-and-thatch cabins. The people, where any appear, are ordinary humans in plain woven earth-coloured clothes. The forest is lit only by the sun, lanterns and fires; no plant glows. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset, never a caption, label, text or border.
